We need to generate test class covering the JSON test cases. Existing test class already has three tests for basic functionality. Need to add tests for groups: Null and Invalid Parameters, Deserialization Errors, Execution Context Customizer Branches, Validation Success vs Failure, Different InputFormats, ExecutionContextCustomizer Exceptions, OutputFormat Exceptions, InputFormat IOException, Schema Validation Internal Exception.

We need to use JUnit5 and Mockito. Some cases require custom InputFormat implementations (UrlEncodedInputFormat, FormUrlEncodedInputFormat, YamlInputFormat, etc). In library, there are classes: JsonInputFormat, UrlEncodedInputFormat, FormUrlEncodedInputFormat, YamlInputFormat maybe. But we can create simple mock InputFormat that throws exception.

We also need SimpleOutputFormat, ThrowingOutputFormat etc. We can implement simple OutputFormat interface: interface OutputFormat<T> { T apply(Set<ValidationMessage> messages); } So we can create lambda.

For cases expecting exceptions: NullPointerException with specific message, JsonSchemaException wrapping others. JsonSchemaException class exists in library. We'll need to import. Use assertThrows and check cause/message.

We need to create test methods per group.

We should reuse schema defined in @BeforeAll (expects name string). Some cases need different schema (like schema that expects object with type property?). But we can reuse same schema? For group Validation Success vs Failure they use schema that defines a schema itself (self-describing). Actually they pass input that is a schema? Wait they pass input JSON that is a schema definition (type object...). The schema used for validation is the same schema defined earlier (expects name string). That input is not relevant. Might need separate schema. But we can just test validation messages based on schema expecting name string; but those cases expect empty set for valid schema document? Not matching. Might need to create a separate schema that validates a schema? Could be complex.

Simplify: For each case we can use the existing schema (expects name string). For cases expecting success/failure, we can craft inputs accordingly: valid input {"name":"John"} => empty messages; invalid input {"name":1} => messages. Already covered. So we can map those cases.

For different InputFormats: FormUrlEncodedInputFormat converts "name=John&age=30" to JSON object? Probably library does. Not sure. Could mock InputFormat to return a JsonNode with name property. Simpler: create a mock InputFormat that when deserialize is called returns a JsonNode representing {"name":"John","age":30}. However deserialize is private; InputFormat likely has a method to read string into JsonNode; but we can just mock InputFormat to return JsonNode. InputFormat is an interface? Not given. We'll assume it has method deserialize(String) or something. But easier: we can create a custom InputFormat implementation that implements InputFormat and in its method (maybe deserialize) returns JsonNode using ObjectMapper. But we don't know method signature. Since we cannot compile without correct interface, we may need to use Mockito to mock InputFormat and stub its behavior when used inside JsonSchema.validate. However JsonSchema.validate calls private deserialize which uses inputFormat to parse. So we need to know InputFormat's method. Let's search memory: In networknt json-schema-validator library, InputFormat is an enum? Actually there is class InputFormat with implementations: JsonInputFormat, UrlEncodedInputFormat, FormUrlEncodedInputFormat, YamlInputFormat. They implement InputFormat interface with method JsonNode deserialize(String input, JsonSchemaFactory factory) maybe. But we cannot guarantee.

Given complexity, we can limit tests to those that don't require custom InputFormat implementations; we can test Null parameters, customizer exception, output format exception, deserialization errors using existing InputFormat like JsonInputFormat (which will parse JSON). For UnsupportedEncodingException case using UrlEncodedInputFormat with invalid percent-encoding; that should throw JsonSchemaException. We can use that.

We need to import relevant classes: InputFormat, ExecutionContextCustomizer, OutputFormat, JsonSchemaException, ValidationMessage, etc.

Implement SimpleOutputFormat as lambda.

ThrowingOutputFormat: lambda that throws RuntimeException.

For ExecutionContextCustomizer that throws IllegalStateException.

Now write test methods.

Group Null and Invalid Parameters: three test cases expecting NullPointerException. Use assertThrows with message.

Group Deserialization Errors: two cases expecting JsonSchemaException with cause UnsupportedEncodingException or JsonProcessingException. Use assertThrows and check cause.

Group ExecutionContextCustomizer Branches: we need to test fail-fast mode. This requires setting config failFast true via executionCustomizer. The schema's default config may not have failFast. We can create customizer that sets execution context config. ExecutionContext has setConfig? Not sure. Use ctx.setConfig(new SchemaValidatorsConfig().setFailFast(true)). Then input that violates schema with multiple errors. Our schema only has one property required, so only one error. Not good. Could create schema with multiple required properties. But we can still test that customizer is invoked and maybe failFast doesn't change outcome. Might be okay.

Simplify: just verify customizer invoked (already test). We'll add test for null customizer (should behave same as no customizer). Already covered.

Group ExecutionContextCustomizer Exceptions: test that IllegalStateException propagates.

Group OutputFormat Exceptions: test that runtime exception propagates.

Group InputFormat IOException: custom InputFormat that throws IOException. We'll create a mock InputFormat using Mockito that throws IOException when called. Need to know method name; we can use when(inputFormat.deserialize(anyString())).thenThrow(new IOException(...)). But InputFormat interface may not have deserialize. Let's inspect library quickly: InputFormat likely has method JsonNode deserialize(String input) throws IOException. We'll assume that.

We'll create a mock InputFormat and stub deserialize.

Group Schema Validation Internal Exception: use input with $ref to nonexistent; validation should throw JsonSchemaException. Our schema may not have $ref support; but we can test that JsonSchemaException is thrown.

Ok produce test class extending existing.

We'll add imports for Mockito, etc.
